key_insight: Pressure enables intercrystalline welding in cellulose at ambient temperature, creating continuous crystalline interfaces and strong bulk materials without solvent-based processing.
engineering_relevance: Powder metallurgy-inspired consolidation offers a route to high-strength cellulose bulk components as potential alternatives to conventional plastics.
method: Use high-speed mechanical pulverization to fibrillate cellulose and increase interlocking and crystalline welding sites.
Consolidate under pressure to transform cellulose I through a transient amorphous state into cellulose II while reconstructing hydrogen bonds.
Combine structural characterization and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate welding and moisture effects.
evidence_signal: The optimized sample, prepared with 40 min fibrillation and 900 MPa molding pressure, reached 72 MPa tensile strength and 667 MPa compressive strength; 5% moisture favored hydrogen-bond rearrangement.
watch_item: The 900 MPa molding pressure raises equipment and scale-up concerns; production feasibility is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Pressure-mediated intercrystalline welding of cellulose via a powder metallurgy-inspired approach for high-strength bulk materials
